report.summary: Chunk 3 of 5: Env site scanning, fallback evidence, registry keys, param switches, and config flatten utility.

handoff.purpose: Implement fallback evidence, state classification, module scanning, registry env keys, param switches, and config flattening.

symbols.name: _fallback_evidence
symbols.note: Returns evidence string if unset variable has a fallback; otherwise empty string.

symbols.name: _mentions
symbols.note: Checks if AST node mentions a given name.

symbols.name: _contains
symbols.note: Checks if haystack AST contains needle AST node by identity.

symbols.name: _statement_for
symbols.note: Returns the innermost enclosing statement from parents list.

symbols.name: _block_for
symbols.note: Returns the block list containing the given statement from parents.

symbols.name: _state_for
symbols.note: Determines state string (REQUIRED, ON, OFF) based on required flag and default literal.

symbols.name: _polarity
symbols.note: Returns 'disable' if name contains inverting tokens, else 'enable'.

symbols.name: _gates_sentence
symbols.note: Returns a human-readable sentence describing what the env var gates.

symbols.name: _collect_module
symbols.note: Parses a Python module file and returns _ModuleInfo or error.

symbols.name: _scan_module
symbols.note: Scans a module for env reads, registry keys, and param switches.

symbols.name: _registry_env_keys
symbols.note: Extracts env_key/env_keys from keyword or dict nodes.

symbols.name: _string_values
symbols.note: Extracts string values from constant, tuple, list, or set nodes.

symbols.name: _param_switches
symbols.note: Extracts boolean parameters that act as feature switches.

symbols.name: _flatten
symbols.note: Flattens nested dict into dotted key-value pairs, skipping keys starting with underscore.

claims.text: Evidence, in order: a DEFAULT-named constant in the same statement; the read sitting in a non-final ``or`` operand (something else answers when it is empty); a conditional expression; or -- when the read is stashed in a local -- a later statement in the same block that consumes that local through a DEFAULT constant, an ``if/else``, or a conditional expression.
claims.why: The function implements exactly these checks: DEFAULT constant, left operand of `or`, conditional expression, and downstream guards on local variable via DEFAULT, if/else, or conditional expression.

claims.text: The guard must be ABOUT this local. Any `or`/`if` anywhere in a long statement that merely happens to mention it is not evidence -- that loose form silently un-darkened three provider API keys.
claims.why: The code checks `_mentions(sub.test, local)` for IfExp and If, and `_mentions(operand, local)` for BoolOp, ensuring the guard is about the local.

claims.text: Non-literal default (a module constant or an expression): a value is supplied, so the feature is configured even when the env is unset.
claims.why: The function returns 'ON' when `has_default_expr` is True and default_literal is None.

claims.text: Registry-declared env keys: `env_key="X"` / `env_keys=("X", ...)`, read later through a variable. Without these the provider lanes look unconfigurable because no literal name appears at the read site.
claims.why: The code iterates over _registry_env_keys(node) and creates EnvSite entries with via='registry'.
The function skips keys that start with underscore via `if str(key).startswith("_"): continue`.

observations.what: In _fallback_evidence, the check for DEFAULT constant in downstream block uses ast.Module(body=sub.body) which is a hack; it may miss some cases.
In _scan_module, the variable 'via' is assigned but never used after the EnvSite creation; it's just stored.
The function _registry_env_keys only handles keyword nodes and dict nodes; it does not handle other patterns like function calls.
In _param_switches, the annotation check requires 'bool' in annotation string; this is fragile for type aliases.
